advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Preserve partial verdicts on the abort path (e.g. hoist `verdicts` to module scope or merge it into the abort marker) so verdicts.json reflects work done before the failure.
evidence: The raw `_EVIDENCE` round trips (global) ARE preserved, but partial verdicts computed before a mid-run SystemExit are not.
advisory.finding: On the SystemExit abort path, `_write_evidence({"aborted": str(exc)})` writes verdicts.json containing only the abort marker; any verdicts already recorded in `main()`'s local `verdicts` dict before the failing step (e.g. `setup_epic_link_write`) are discarded because that dict is not reachable from the handler.
scenarios: A run that writes the Epic Link successfully, records setup_epic_link_write, then aborts at read-back (line 155) — verdicts.json shows only {"aborted": ...}, dropping the OK verdict.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Signal truncation in the 'names present' log (e.g. append '(first 40 of N)') so a large inventory is not silently clipped.
evidence: 105:             "  field %r absent from an inventory of %d field(s); names present: %s",
108:             sorted({str(f.get("name")) for f in body if isinstance(f, dict)})[:40],
The inventory size (%d) is logged, so a reader can infer truncation only by comparing count to the printed list length.
advisory.finding: The 'names present' diagnostic sorts the full field-name set and then truncates to 40 (`sorted({...})[:40]`) but the log message does not indicate truncation, so a field present under a slightly different alphabetically-late name would appear absent to an operator reading the log.
scenarios: A Jira instance with >40 fields where a near-miss name (e.g. 'Epic-Link') sorts past position 40 — the log omits it, masking the actual cause the diagnostic was added to surface.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the handler-side `_write_evidence` calls so a write failure is logged but the original exception still propagates.
evidence: No guard around the `_write_evidence` call in either handler; a write error there replaces the original SystemExit/exception.
advisory.finding: If `_write_evidence` raises inside the SystemExit or Exception handler (e.g. OUT_DIR mkdir/write_text fails), the new exception masks the original failure, defeating the change's stated goal of preserving diagnostics on any exit.
scenarios: Read-only or full output directory, or a permission error on OUT_DIR — the operator sees the write error, not the underlying probe failure the evidence was meant to explain.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that stubs `_req`/urlopen to force a `PROBE SETUP FAILED` SystemExit and asserts `evidence.json` and `verdicts.json` exist under `JIRA_DC_PROBE_OUTPUT_DIR` after the abort (and similarly for the unexpected-exception path).
evidence: scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:233-240 `except SystemExit as exc: _write_evidence({"aborted": str(exc)}) ... raise` — new failure-path evidence write, untested
scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:241-244 `except Exception as exc: _write_evidence({"crashed": repr(exc)}) ... raise` — new crash-path evidence write, untested
The only tests naming the script assert workflow YAML text, not probe behavior: tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py:146 `assert "jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py" in text`

ABSENCE: search for `_write_evidence`, `evidence.json`, and `JIRA_DC_PROBE_OUTPUT_DIR` across the repo returns only the script itself and workflow/YAML-parity tests — no test exercises `main()` or `_write_evidence` on any exit path.
Ticket 4b9e comment PROBE-4B9E-R1 documents the regression this fixes: `PROBE SETUP FAILED ... No files were found with the provided path` — a concrete, reproducible failure path.
advisory.finding: The change's central fix — that evidence (`evidence.json`) is now persisted on the SystemExit setup-failure path and on unexpected-exception paths — is a deterministic, unit-testable behavior with a concrete, already-observed failure history, yet ships with no unit test. The exact regression it repairs (setup failure discards the one diagnostic artifact) could silently return with no guard.
scenarios: A future edit reorders the evidence write back inside/after `main()` and setup again fails at field discovery, silently discarding evidence — no test fails.
The `_field_id` unusable-inventory vs absent-field diagnostic branches (lines 90-110) regress to a bare `None` again with no assertion catching it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit/test_jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py: monkeypatch `_req` to append to `_EVIDENCE` then raise SystemExit at field discovery, set `JIRA_DC_PROBE_OUTPUT_DIR` to `tmp_path`, run the `__main__` guard (or call `_write_evidence` via the same path), and assert `(tmp_path/'evidence.json').exists()` and its parsed contents contain the recorded round trips plus the `aborted` verdict; add a parallel case raising a non-SystemExit exception asserting the `crashed` verdict.
